Abbathor

God of greed

Overview

TitleGod of greed
EpithetsThe Great Master of Greed, The Trove Wyrm
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Evil (NE)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA jewelled dagger, point down
Home planeHades
Typical worshippersGreedy dwarves, dwarven thieves, unscrupulous merchants

Description

Abbathor is the dark side of the dwarves' love of gold and gems: the greed that drives them to steal, betray and hoard without end. He is still part of the dwarven pantheon, because the other gods acknowledge that this desire exists in every dwarf. Offerings are sometimes made to him when a treasure is found, so that he does not push a companion to betrayal.

Dogma

Wealth is the only true measure of worth. Hoard, jealously guard what you own and take what you desire, by cunning if need be.

The faithful

Abbathor's faithful are greedy, secretive and wary of everyone, including those close to them. They count and recount their treasure, hide it in places nobody knows and see each gem as an offering. They do not hesitate to rob a companion, falsify a share or break a contract if the gain is worth it. Their rites take place alone, before a hidden treasure, by candlelight. Most dwarves do not really worship him, but leave a small gem for him when they make a find, so that he pushes no one to betrayal.

Aerdrie Faenya

Goddess of the sky

Overview

TitleGoddess of the sky
EpithetsThe Queen of Air and Weather, The Lady of Winged Creatures
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsTempest, Trickery
SymbolA bird silhouetted against a cloud
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersAvariels, air elves, sky travellers

Description

Aerdrie Faenya is the elven goddess of air, weather and winged creatures. Independent and unpredictable, she loves freedom and change. She is especially revered by the avariels, the winged elves. She is the mother of flying creatures, and her faithful love flight and adventure.

Dogma

Freedom is the greatest of gifts. Fly, follow your desires and never let yourself be caged.

The faithful

Aerdrie's faithful are free, unpredictable and in love with the sky. They watch birds, read the clouds and forecast the weather. Many are avariels, the winged elves, or elves who raise flying mounts. They refuse to stay long in one place and despise cages, which they open as soon as they find one. Their rites take place on clifftops, where birds are released as offerings. They believe freedom is the greatest of gifts and that change is natural.

Akadi

Goddess of air

Overview

TitleGoddess of air
EpithetsThe Queen of the Air, The Lady of Air, She Who Is the Wind
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsTempest
SymbolA cloud
Home planeElemental Plane of Air
Typical worshippersSky travellers, aeronauts, air genasi, free spirits

Description

Akadi is one of the four great elemental powers worshipped in Faerûn. She embodies air in all its forms: the cooling breeze, the overturning gust, the breath that carries the birds. Changeable and elusive, she cares little for the affairs of mortals and has no organised church, but sailors, breeders of flying mounts and those who live at altitude readily say a prayer to her before setting out.

Dogma

Freedom of movement is sacred. Nothing should stay still or locked away; travelling, changing your mind and following your impulse are virtues.

The faithful

Akadi's faithful hate putting down roots. They often change trade, town or opinion, and consider stillness a sickness of the soul. They build no temples: they pray in the open wind, on hilltops or on the decks of ships, and let feathers, ribbons or ashes fly away as offerings. Their few priests are wanderers who act as mediators between factions. They are known for being cheerful but unreliable, because to their eyes promising to stay is a betrayal of their goddess.

Amaunator

God of the sun

Overview

TitleGod of the sun
EpithetsThe Keeper of the Eternal Sun, The Light of Law, The Yellow God
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsLife, Light
SymbolA golden sun
Home planeMechanus
Typical worshippersFarmers, lawmakers, travellers

Description

An ancient sun deity of the empire of Netheril, Amaunator is the sun seen as an unchanging law: it always rises and sets on time. Long thought to have vanished, his cult resurfaced in the century of the Wars of Magic, and many believe he is one with Lathander, being his most rigid and oldest aspect. His temples keep registers, calendars and contracts, for he is also the god of written order and bureaucracy.

Dogma

Law is as constant as the course of the sun. Commitments must be kept, rules applied and time respected.

The faithful

Amaunator's faithful live by the clock and the calendar. They rise with the sun, pray at dawn, noon and dusk, and consider punctuality a religious virtue. They are people of archives and procedures: they draw up contracts, keep land registers and readily serve as notaries or magistrates. Their temples, with golden roofs facing east, often contain a monumental sundial and archive rooms. They judge harshly those who break their word, and are often rigid in the face of exceptions.

Angharradh

Triple goddess of wisdom and protection

Overview

TitleTriple goddess of wisdom and protection
EpithetsThe Queen of Arvandor, The Triune Goddess
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsKnowledge, Life, Peace
SymbolA triangle containing three interlocking circles
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersElves, protectors, healers

Description

Angharradh is an elven goddess formed from the fusion of three goddesses: Aerdrie Faenya, Hanali Celanil and Sehanine Moonbow. She embodies wisdom, protection, fertility and growth. She is Corellon's consort and the queen of Arvandor. Her faithful protect elven communities and encourage them to flourish.

Dogma

The elven people must be protected and nurtured. Cultivate wisdom, defend your own and encourage growth.

The faithful

Angharradh's faithful are wise, protective and nurturing. They watch over elven communities, tend the sick, advise leaders and defend their people against danger. Her priestesses often form circles of three, each honouring one aspect of the goddess. They believe wisdom, growth and protection are the three pillars of a people's survival. Their rites celebrate births, harvests and alliances, and take place in sacred gardens.

Arvoreen

God of vigilance and war

Overview

TitleGod of vigilance and war
EpithetsThe Defender, The Vigilant Guardian
PantheonHalfling pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolTwo crossed short swords
Home planeBytopia (Green Fields)
Typical worshippersHalfling warriors, guards

Description

Arvoreen is the halfling god of defence and vigilance. He protects halfling communities from outside dangers. His faithful are warriors and guards who defend their people. He is serious and devoted.

Dogma

Vigilance protects the community. Stand guard, defend your own and be ready to fight.

The faithful

Arvoreen's faithful are vigilant, serious and devoted. They protect their community from outside dangers, organise patrols and train the young in combat. They are more solemn than most halflings. They believe vigilance protects the community. Their rites include guard vigils and oaths of protection.

Asmodeus

God of indulgence and lord of the Nine Hells

Overview

TitleGod of indulgence and lord of the Nine Hells
EpithetsThe Cloven, The Lord of the Ninth, Old Hoof and Horn
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Evil (LE)
Suggested domainsKnowledge, Trickery, Order
SymbolThree inverted triangles arranged in a long triangle
Home planeThe Nine Hells (Nessus)
Typical worshippersCorrupt politicians, desperate people, pact signers

Description

Undisputed ruler of the Nine Hells, Asmodeus rose to godhood in Faerûn by seizing the power of a dead god during the Time of Troubles. He does not promise damnation: he offers contracts. Power, wealth, revenge, pleasure — everything can be had for a price, and that price always ends up being the soul. His cult thrives in courts, guilds and wherever ambition outweighs scruples; his most fervent faithful are found in Thay and in some noble houses of the South.

Dogma

Everything has a price and everything can be negotiated. The weak submit, the clever sign good contracts, and one's word binds absolutely.

The faithful

Asmodeus's faithful almost always hide their faith. They think in terms of power and debts: every service rendered creates an obligation, every weakness of others is a lever. They meet in secret hierarchical circles, often disguised as clubs, guilds or charitable societies. There, pacts drafted with extreme legal care are signed, and those who recruit new signatories are rewarded. They are polite, patient and methodical; open violence seems vulgar to them, for a good contract is far more effective than a blade.

Auril

Goddess of winter

Overview

TitleGoddess of winter
EpithetsThe Frostmaiden, Lady Frostkiss, Icedawn
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Evil (NE)
Suggested domainsNature, Tempest
SymbolA six-pointed snowflake
Home planePandemonium (Pandesmos)
Typical worshippersDruids, inhabitants of cold lands

Description

Auril is winter at its most merciless: the cold that kills beasts, the blizzard that leads travellers astray, the ice that freezes rivers. Vain and cruel, she demands offerings to spare villages, and the people of Icewind Dale fear her more than they love her. She serves Talos alongside Umberlee and Malar, and her faithful say she can freeze a mortal's heart with a single glance.

Dogma

Cold reveals the true nature of things: only the strong survive the winter. Fear Auril, appease her with offerings and spread ice upon those who scorn her.

The faithful

Auril's worshippers live in fear and respect of winter. In the northern regions, entire villages leave offerings of food and extinguished fire at the edge of the snow, or sometimes sacrifice a stranger during the worst storms. Her true faithful are hard, cold and scornful of comfort: they sleep without fire, walk barefoot in the snow and look down on those who complain of the cold. Their shrines are ice caves or circles of frosted stones. They celebrate the first snow and the longest night of the year.

Azuth

God of wizards

Overview

TitleGod of wizards
EpithetsThe High One, The Lord of Spells, The Shining Hand of Sorcery
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsArcana, Knowledge
SymbolA left hand pointing upward, surrounded by flames
Home planeArcadia (Buxenus)
Typical worshippersArcane spellcasters, wizards

Description

Azuth was once a mortal, a wizard so accomplished that he became Mystra's first Chosen before rising to godhood himself. Today he is the servant of the Lady of Mysteries and the patron of those who study magic with rigour. Where Mystra is the Weave itself, Azuth is the method: patient learning, the memorisation of formulas and the passing on of arcane knowledge from master to student. He is often depicted as a wise old man with a mocking gaze.

Dogma

Magic is an art that is learned, practised and taught. Use it with intelligence and caution, record your discoveries and train the next generation.

The faithful

Azuth's faithful are studious, methodical and a little pedantic. They revere precision: a well-cast spell is a prayer, a well-kept spellbook an act of faith. They found schools of magic, hold theoretical debates and take teaching very seriously, each master being bound to train at least one apprentice. During rituals, they raise their left hand like their god. They distrust the instinctive magic of sorcerers and those who cast spells without understanding them, which they consider dangerous to all.

Baervan Wildwanderer

God of the woods

Overview

TitleGod of the woods
EpithetsThe Forest Wanderer, The Masked Leaf
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsNature
SymbolA raccoon's face
Home planeBytopia (Golden Hills)
Typical worshippersForest gnomes, rangers, druids

Description

Baervan Wildwanderer is the gnomish god of forests, travel and nature. He is accompanied by a giant raccoon named Chiktikka. He protects forest gnomes and woodland creatures. His faithful are gnomish rangers and druids.

Dogma

The forest is a friend to be protected. Travel, explore and live in harmony with nature.

The faithful

Baervan's faithful are forest gnomes close to nature and animals. They explore the woods, protect wild creatures and live discreetly in hidden burrows. Many have an animal companion, often a raccoon. They believe the forest is a friend that must be respected. Their rites take place in the wild, in clearings, with songs and offerings of nuts and berries.

Bahgtru

God of strength

Overview

TitleGod of strength
EpithetsThe Bonebreaker, The Son of Gruumsh
PantheonOrc pantheon
AlignmentLawful Evil (LE)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolA broken thighbone
Home planeAcheron (Nishrek)
Typical worshippersOrc warriors, wrestlers

Description

Bahgtru is the orc god of brute strength. Son of Gruumsh and Luthic, he is loyal but not very intelligent. He embodies physical power. His faithful are warriors who favour strength over strategy.

Dogma

Strength is the only law. Crush your enemies and prove your might.

The faithful

Bahgtru's faithful are orc warriors who value brute strength above all. They fight bare-handed, break bones as a sign of power and despise cunning. They believe strength is the only law. Their rites include trials of strength and ritual fights.

Bane

God of tyranny

Overview

TitleGod of tyranny
EpithetsThe Black Hand, The Lord of Darkness
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Evil (LE)
Suggested domainsWar, Order
SymbolAn upright black hand, thumb and fingers together
Home planeAcheron (Avalas)
Typical worshippersConquerors, fighters, monks, tyrants

Description

Bane is the god of domination, fear and organised hatred. He does not preach chaos: he wants a world where everyone is in their place, under the rule of a single master. A member of the Dark Three with Bhaal and Myrkul, he has died and returned several times over the centuries, which strengthens his faithful's conviction that he is inevitable. His hierarchical and military Church is powerful around the Moonsea, in Zhentil Keep and in every city ruled with an iron fist.

Dogma

Power belongs to those who seize it. Fear is the tool of order, submission is owed to the strongest, and Bane's will must spread across all of Faerûn.

The faithful

Bane's faithful believe the world is a hierarchy and that their place is at the top. They are disciplined, obedient to their superiors and ruthless towards their subordinates. Their Church works like an army: ranks, black uniforms, written reports, exemplary punishments. They infiltrate city councils, fund mercenaries and encourage authoritarian rulers. Their ceremonies stage submission, often with oaths sworn with the right hand on an iron black hand. They despise pity, which they see as a luxury of the weak.

Baravar Cloakshadow

God of illusion and deception

Overview

TitleGod of illusion and deception
EpithetsThe Lord of Illusions, The Sly One
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsArcana, Trickery
SymbolA dagger in front of a hooded cloak
Home planeBytopia (Golden Hills)
Typical worshippersGnomish illusionists, rogues

Description

Baravar Cloakshadow is the gnomish god of illusion, cunning and protection. He uses his illusions to protect gnomes from their enemies. His faithful are illusionists and rogues who use cunning rather than force.

Dogma

Cunning is more powerful than force. Master illusion, protect your people and deceive your enemies.

The faithful

Baravar's faithful are cunning, discreet and protective. They master illusion and use it to hide their communities, deceive their enemies and avoid fights. They believe cunning is more powerful than force and that a deceived enemy is a defeated enemy. They set traps and illusions around their burrows. Their rites include displays of illusion and games of deception.

Berronar Truesilver

Goddess of hearth and home

Overview

TitleGoddess of hearth and home
EpithetsThe Revered Mother, The Mother Safe
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsLife, Light, Peace
SymbolTwo interlocking silver rings
Home planeMount Celestia (Erackinor)
Typical worshippersMothers, keepers of the hearth, dwarven healers

Description

Moradin's wife, Berronar is the goddess of hearth, loyalty, marriage and safety. She watches over dwarven families, the memory of bloodlines and exchanged oaths. Her priests celebrate marriages, keep genealogies and tend the wounded. For dwarves, she represents everything that makes a fortress a true home.

Dogma

The clan is a family and the family is sacred. Keep your oaths, protect the hearth and keep the memory of the ancestors alive.

The faithful

Berronar's faithful are protective, loyal and devoted to family above all. They celebrate marriages with the exchange of two silver rings, keep the clan's genealogies up to date and make sure no orphan is left without a home. They hold an oath to be sacred: breaking it dishonours one's whole bloodline. Priestesses often act as the living memory of the clan and settle family disputes. Rites take place at the hearth, around the fire, and every traveller's return is celebrated with a shared meal. To them, a fortress without united families is just a pile of stones.

Beshaba

Goddess of misfortune

Overview

TitleGoddess of misfortune
EpithetsLady Doom, The Maid of Misfortune
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolBlack deer antlers
Home planeThe Abyss
Typical worshippersGamblers, Red Wizards, rogues

Description

Twin sister and rival of Tymora, Beshaba is bad luck personified: the slipping foot, the snapping rope, the coin landing on the wrong side. The people of Faerûn call on her less to win her favour than to avoid her attention, and many cross their fingers or make a ritual gesture when misfortune looms. Her few priests sell protection against accidents… which they sometimes cause themselves.

Dogma

Misfortune strikes everyone; better to fear and respect it than to defy it. Those who honour Beshaba may be spared.

The faithful

Most people who pray to Beshaba do so out of superstition: they avoid naming the goddess, spit on the ground after bad news, hang blackened antlers above doors. Her true faithful are few and resemble spiritual racketeers: they “protect” against accidents in exchange for offerings, and cause misfortune for those who refuse to pay. They believe the world is cruel by nature and that it is better to be on the side of bad luck than to suffer it. They avoid the temples of Tymora, which they consider naive.

Bhaal

God of murder

Overview

TitleGod of murder
EpithetsThe Lord of Murder
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Evil (NE)
Suggested domainsDeath
SymbolA skull surrounded by a ring of blood drops
Home planeGehenna (Khalas)
Typical worshippersAssassins, murderers

Description

Bhaal is the power of murder, not of natural death but of life torn away by violence. A member of the Dark Three, he perished during the Time of Troubles and left behind many mortal children, the Bhaalspawn, whose story shook the Sword Coast. Having since returned, he inspires secret cults that practise ritual assassination; in Baldur's Gate, his name remains synonymous with nightmare.

Dogma

Every life is an offering in waiting. Murder is a sacred act, and every violent death feeds the power of the Lord of Murder.

The faithful

Bhaal's faithful live in absolute secrecy, organised in small cells that barely know each other. They consider each murder an offering and compete in ingenuity in staging it: they often draw a circle of blood around the victim's body. Some cults carry out assassinations to order; others kill out of pure devotion. They often lead a double life that looks very respectable. Their thinking is cold and fatalistic: other people's lives only have value as a sacrifice, and the fear they inspire is a form of prayer.

Brandobaris

God of thievery and adventure

Overview

TitleGod of thievery and adventure
EpithetsThe Master of Stealth, The Wanderer
PantheonHalfling pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA halfling's footprint
Home planeBytopia (Green Fields)
Typical worshippersHalfling rogues, adventurers, travellers

Description

Brandobaris is the halfling god of adventure, stealth and thievery. He embodies curiosity and a taste for risk. His faithful are adventurers and rogues who love to explore and discover new horizons.

Dogma

Curiosity is a virtue. Explore, take risks and always find a way out.

The faithful

Brandobaris's faithful are curious, bold and stealthy. They explore, take risks and always find a way out of tight spots. Many are adventurers or rogues. They believe curiosity is a virtue and that one must see the world. Their rites are tales of adventure told around the fire.

Callarduran Smoothhands

God of mining and stone carving

Overview

TitleGod of mining and stone carving
EpithetsThe Master of Stone, The Lord of the Underdark
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsKnowledge, Nature
SymbolA gold signet ring bearing a six-pointed star
Home planeBytopia (Golden Hills)
Typical worshippersDeep gnomes, miners, stonecutters

Description

Callarduran Smoothhands is the gnomish god of stone, mines and the Underdark. He is especially revered by the svirfneblin, the deep gnomes. He protects miners and teaches the art of cutting stone. He is the enemy of Laduguer and Urdlen.

Dogma

Stone holds treasures for those who know how to work it. Dig with care, protect the depths and respect the earth.

The faithful

Callarduran's faithful are hard-working, patient deep gnomes. They dig tunnels, cut stone with great finesse and protect their underground cities from the dangers of the Underdark. They believe stone holds treasures for those who know how to work it. They distrust duergar and drow. Their rites take place in sacred caverns where carved stones are offered.

Chauntea

Goddess of agriculture

Overview

TitleGoddess of agriculture
EpithetsThe Grain Goddess, The Great Mother
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsLife
SymbolA sheaf of grain, or a blooming rose over grain
Home planeElysium (Eronia)
Typical worshippersFarmers, gardeners, settlers

Description

Chauntea is the cultivated earth and the life it gives: ploughed fields, orchards, harvests brought in. Beloved by peasants throughout Faerûn, she is one of the most widely prayed-to deities, even by those who attend no temple. Her priests bless the sowing, help with the harvest and share practical knowledge about soils and seasons. She is naturally opposed to Talos and Auril, who destroy crops, and has a complex relationship with Silvanus, who prefers wild nature.

Dogma

Tilling the earth is a sacred act. Plant, tend, share the fruits of the harvest and never waste what the earth has given.

The faithful

Chauntea's faithful are simple, patient and practical people, attached to the land and the rhythm of the seasons. They pray before sowing, bless the first ears of grain and hold great harvest festivals where the meal is shared with travellers. They never waste food and readily give to the hungry. Their priests are often farmers themselves: they advise on crops, help with harvests and settle boundary disputes. They distrust destroyers, storms and wars that trample the fields.

Clangeddin Silverbeard

God of war

Overview

TitleGod of war
EpithetsThe Father of Battle, The Lord of the Twin Axes
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolTwo crossed silver battleaxes
Home planeArcadia
Typical worshippersDwarven warriors, soldiers, strategists

Description

Clangeddin is the dwarven god of war, bravery and honour in battle. He is depicted as an old scarred warrior wielding two axes. He despises cowardice and urges dwarves to fight to the end to defend their clan. He harbours a particular hatred of giants, orcs and goblins.

Dogma

Battle is an honour. Face the enemy with courage, never abandon a companion and never retreat before the enemies of the dwarven people.

The faithful

Clangeddin's faithful are proud warriors who live by a strict code of honour. They train every day, maintain their weapons with religious care and sing long war songs that list the deeds of the ancestors. They believe it is better to die standing than live on one's knees, and that a dwarf never retreats when the clan is threatened. They harbour a stubborn hatred of giants, orcs and goblins. Before a battle, they hold a vigil of arms and swear an oath on two crossed axes; afterwards, they carve the names of the dead in stone.

Corellon Larethian

God of art and magic

Overview

TitleGod of art and magic
EpithetsThe Creator, The Protector, The First of the Seldarine
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsArcana, Light
SymbolA crescent moon
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersElves, artists, wizards, bards

Description

Corellon is the leader of the Seldarine, the elven pantheon, and the creator of the elves, who are said to have been born from the blood he shed in his fight against Gruumsh. He embodies magic, art, music and beauty. A changeable deity, he has no fixed form and can be male, female or both. He protects his people against the orcs and against Lolth, who once betrayed him.

Dogma

Art and magic are the essence of elven life. Create, protect your people and live with freedom and grace.

The faithful

Corellon's faithful are artists, wizards and refined warriors. They cultivate beauty in everything they do, from poetry to swordplay, and believe elven life must be lived with grace and freedom. They readily accept those who change their appearance or identity, for their god has no fixed form. They protect their people against orcs and drow, and hold great festivals under the moon with songs, dances and displays of magic. They hate tyranny and anything that cages the mind.

Cyric

God of lies

Overview

TitleGod of lies
EpithetsThe Black Sun, The Prince of Lies
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA jawless white skull on a black or purple sun
Home planePandemonium (Cocytus)
Typical worshippersLiars, manipulators, the power-hungry

Description

A mortal who became a god during the Time of Troubles, Cyric seized the portfolios of Bane, Bhaal and Myrkul before partly losing them. Unstable, jealous and consumed by ambition, he is the god of deceit, plots and madness. He hates most other gods and has been imprisoned or punished several times for his schemes. His cult attracts those who want everything and will stop at no betrayal to get it.

Dogma

Truth is only a lie that succeeded. All other gods are impostors; sow doubt, break alliances and trust only Cyric.

The faithful

Cyric's faithful are paranoid, ambitious and often unstable. They trust no one, not even their brothers in faith, and infighting is the norm in his temples. They spread rumours, forge documents, turn allies against each other and delight in seeing others' work collapse. They consider that all other gods lie and that only Cyric tells the truth. Their rites include readings from the “Cyrinishad”, a contradictory and deranged text that everyone interprets in their own way.

Cyrrollalee

Goddess of hearth and home

Overview

TitleGoddess of hearth and home
EpithetsThe Friendly Hand, The Faithful One
PantheonHalfling pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsLife, Peace
SymbolAn open door
Home planeBytopia (Green Fields)
Typical worshippersHalflings, hosts, innkeepers

Description

Cyrrollalee is the halfling goddess of hospitality, friendship and the home. She encourages welcoming travellers and helping one's neighbours. Her faithful are innkeepers and hosts who welcome all who need it.

Dogma

Hospitality is sacred. Welcome travellers, help your neighbours and cultivate friendship.

The faithful

Cyrrollalee's faithful are welcoming, friendly and generous. They welcome travellers, help their neighbours and cultivate friendship. Many run inns. They believe hospitality is sacred and that an open door is a prayer. Their rites take place around a shared meal.

Deep Duerra

Duergar goddess of conquest and psionics

Overview

TitleDuergar goddess of conquest and psionics
EpithetsThe Queen of the Invisible Legions, Daughter of Laduguer
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentLawful Evil (LE)
Suggested domainsArcana, War
SymbolA mind flayer skull
Home planeAcheron
Typical worshippersDuergar, psionicists, conquerors

Description

Duerra is the duergar goddess of expansion, conquest and psionic powers. Daughter of Laduguer, she is said to have stolen the secret of mental powers from the mind flayers and passed it on to the duergar. Her faithful want to extend their people's dominion in the Underdark and hunt illithids relentlessly.

Dogma

The mind is the ultimate weapon. Develop your mental powers, conquer new territories and destroy the mind flayers.

The faithful

Duerra's faithful are ambitious, disciplined duergar convinced that their people must dominate the Underdark. They develop their psionic powers through gruelling mental exercises and organise raids against neighbouring cities. They hunt mind flayers with a particular obsession and collect their skulls as trophies. Their thinking is cold and expansionist: every conquered territory proves the superiority of the duergar mind. Their ceremonies are displays of mental power before prisoners, often followed by planning the next conquest.

Deep Sashelas

God of the sea

Overview

TitleGod of the sea
EpithetsThe Dolphin Prince, The Creator of the Sea Elves
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsNature
SymbolA dolphin
Home planeArborea
Typical worshippersSea elves, elven sailors

Description

Deep Sashelas is the elven god of the sea and the oceans. He protects sea elves and marine creatures, and favours knowledge and creation. He opposes Sekolah, the god of the sahuagin. His faithful are mostly sea elves, but also elven sailors who travel the seas.

Dogma

The sea is a source of life and knowledge. Protect its creatures, explore its depths and fight those who threaten it.

The faithful

Sashelas's faithful are sea elves who are curious, creative and protective of the ocean. They explore the depths, chart the reefs and protect marine creatures, especially dolphins. They fight the sahuagin, enemies of their god, relentlessly. They believe the sea is a source of life and knowledge. Their rites take place underwater, in coral temples, or on beaches at high tide. Surface elven sailors pray to him before putting to sea.

Deneir

God of writing

Overview

TitleGod of writing
EpithetsThe First Scribe, The Lord of All Glyphs and Images, The Scribe of Oghma
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsArcana, Knowledge
SymbolA lit candle above an open eye
Home planeElysium (Amoria)
Typical worshippersSages, scribes, students, teachers

Description

A servant of Oghma, Deneir is the god of the written word: the alphabet, glyphs, calligraphy, illumination and cartography. It is said that he spends eternity reading and transcribing the Metatext, a hidden writing that is said to describe the very structure of the universe. His priests copy and preserve books, teach children to read and keep the archives of many cities. They also protect libraries from those who would burn knowledge.

Dogma

Written knowledge outlives those who produced it. Record, copy, preserve and share the written word, and teach anyone who wishes to read.

The faithful

Deneir's faithful are patient, meticulous scholars. They spend hours copying, illustrating and restoring manuscripts, and see every destroyed book as a small death. They teach reading and writing for free, write letters for the illiterate and keep the records of communities. They often live in great library-temples with silent halls. Their thinking is focused on passing things on: knowledge that is not recorded is knowledge lost. They are wary of those who jealously hoard knowledge.

Dugmaren Brightmantle

God of discovery

Overview

TitleGod of discovery
EpithetsThe Gleam in the Eye, The Wandering Tinker
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsKnowledge
SymbolAn open book
Home planeThe Outlands
Typical worshippersDwarven inventors, scholars, explorers

Description

Dugmaren is the dwarven god of scholarship, discovery and invention. Curious and absent-minded, he urges dwarves to leave the beaten track and experiment. His faithful are researchers, inventors and explorers, often seen as eccentric by other dwarves. He is the son of Moradin and Berronar.

Dogma

Knowledge must be sought tirelessly. Experiment, discover new techniques and share your knowledge with your people.

The faithful

Dugmaren's faithful are curious, inventive and often distracted by their latest idea. They explore old ruins, test new alloys and ask questions the elders find disturbing. Other dwarves often think them eccentric, even disrespectful of tradition. They found libraries and experimental workshops, and readily share their discoveries. Their rites consist of presenting a discovery before the clan, whether it succeeded or not. They believe stagnation kills peoples as surely as war.

Dumathoin

God of buried secrets

Overview

TitleGod of buried secrets
EpithetsThe Keeper of Secrets under the Mountain, The Silent Keeper
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsDeath, Knowledge
SymbolA mountain silhouette with a gem at its centre
Home planeThe Outlands
Typical worshippersMiners, jewellers, keepers of the dead

Description

Dumathoin is the dwarven god of the secrets of the earth, precious metals, gems and the dead. He watches over the riches hidden beneath the mountain and over the tombs of the ancestors. Silent and discreet, he guides miners to the veins and protects the rest of the departed. His priests organise dwarven funerals and fight those who loot tombs.

Dogma

The earth keeps its treasures for those who respect it. Extract riches with care, honour the dead and protect the tombs of the ancestors.

The faithful

Dumathoin's faithful are silent, patient and deeply respectful of the mountain. They guide miners to the veins, learn to read the rock and refuse to work a vein until it is exhausted. They organise dwarven funerals, prepare tombs in the rock and make sure the dead are never disturbed. They hate tomb robbers and those who dig without respect. Their rites take place in the deepest tunnels, in silence or in whispers, and a gem is often placed in the tomb of the deceased.

Eilistraee

Goddess of song and moonlight

Overview

TitleGoddess of song and moonlight
EpithetsThe Dark Maiden, The Lady of the Dance, Lady Silverhair
PantheonDrow pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsLight, Nature
SymbolThe silhouette of a drow dancing with a sword before the full moon
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersBladesingers, elves, performers

Description

Eilistraee is the drow goddess of beauty, song and moonlight. Daughter of Corellon and Araushnee (who would become Lolth), she chose light over darkness and helps drow who want to escape Lolth's tyranny. Her faithful dance under the moon, help the oppressed and hunt monsters. She was killed and then brought back to life in recent events.

Dogma

Beauty and goodness are open to everyone, even the drow. Help those who want to flee the darkness, dance under the moon and fight the servants of Lolth.

The faithful

Eilistraee's faithful dance under the moon, sing and wield the sword with grace. They help drow who want to flee Lolth's tyranny, take in refugees and help them settle on the surface. They organise hunts against monsters and Lolth's servants. They believe beauty and goodness are open to everyone, the drow included. Their rites take place outdoors, at night, with dances and songs. They are often bladesingers or performers.

Eldath

Goddess of peace

Overview

TitleGoddess of peace
EpithetsThe Guardian of Groves, The Quiet One, The Mother of Waters
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsLife, Nature, Peace
SymbolA waterfall plunging into a still pool
Home planeElysium (Eronia)
Typical worshippersDruids, pacifists, the dying

Description

Eldath rules over peaceful places: quiet pools, calm clearings, waterfalls that soothe the mind. She is inner peace as much as peace between peoples. Her faithful are mediators, healers and keepers of natural sanctuaries; many refuse to bear arms, but they stubbornly defend their sacred places with cunning and patience. She is one of the nature gods in the service of Silvanus.

Dogma

Violence is a last resort. Seek peace, offer refuge to the persecuted and protect the places where the soul can rest.

The faithful

Eldath's faithful are calm, gentle and patient. They avoid conflict, always seek compromise and often serve as mediators in quarrels between villages. Many refuse to bear arms and only fight as a last resort, to protect a sacred place. Their sanctuaries are pools, waterfalls and peaceful clearings where they shelter refugees, the sick and the dying. They pray through silent meditation, often near water. Their strength is quiet resistance: they can stand still before an army without yielding an inch.

Erevan Ilesere

God of mischief

Overview

TitleGod of mischief
EpithetsThe Trickster, The Changer
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Neutral (CN)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolAn asymmetrical eight-armed star
Home planeArborea
Typical worshippersPrankster elves, fey, rogues

Description

Erevan Ilesere is the elven god of mischief, pranks and change. Unpredictable and impish, he loves playing tricks, even on the other gods. He is popular among the fey and elves who like to have fun. Despite his pranks, he remains loyal to the Seldarine.

Dogma

Life is too short to be taken seriously. Laugh, play tricks and stay free of all constraints.

The faithful

Erevan's faithful are impish, unpredictable and allergic to rules. They play tricks on everyone, including their loved ones and the authorities, and consider that a good prank deflates the pride of the powerful. They often change their appearance, name or plans. They believe life is too short to be taken seriously and that rules are made to be bent. Their rites are games, pranks and impromptu parties. Even so, they remain loyal to their people in the face of real danger.

Fenmarel Mestarine

God of outcasts

Overview

TitleGod of outcasts
EpithetsThe Lone Wolf
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Neutral (CN)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolTwo watching elven eyes
Home planeArborea
Typical worshippersExiled elves, outcasts, loners

Description

Fenmarel Mestarine is the elven god of exiles, outcasts and loners. He himself lives apart from the other elven gods. He protects those who have been driven out of their community or who have chosen to live alone. His faithful are often wary and independent.

Dogma

Solitude is not a weakness. Learn to survive alone, help the exiled and rely only on yourself.

The faithful

Fenmarel's faithful are solitary, wary and fiercely independent. They are often exiled elves, driven out of their community or gone of their own accord. They live apart, in the deep woods or on the edges of cities. They believe one must know how to survive alone and rely only on oneself. Yet they quietly help other exiles, leaving them supplies or advice. Their rites are individual, silent and without witnesses.

Flandal Steelskin

God of metalwork

Overview

TitleGod of metalwork
EpithetsThe Master of Metal, The Lord of the Forge
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsKnowledge
SymbolA flaming hammer
Home planeBytopia (Golden Hills)
Typical worshippersGnomish smiths, artisans, inventors

Description

Flandal Steelskin is the gnomish god of the forge, metal and craftsmanship. He teaches gnomes the art of forging and inventing. His faithful are smiths and artisans who create objects of great finesse.

Dogma

Well-forged metal lasts forever. Work with care, innovate and pass on your skills.

The faithful

Flandal's faithful are inventive smiths and artisans. They create objects of great finesse and share their techniques with other gnomes. They believe well-forged metal lasts forever and that innovation is a form of prayer. Their rites take place at the forge, where new creations are blessed by plunging them into the fire.

Gaerdal Ironhand

God of protection

Overview

TitleGod of protection
EpithetsThe Shield of the Gnomes, The Guardian
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsWar, Peace
SymbolAn iron band
Home planeBytopia (Golden Hills)
Typical worshippersGnomish warriors, guards, defenders

Description

Gaerdal Ironhand is the gnomish god of vigilance, combat and defence. Stern and serious, he protects gnomish communities from their enemies. His faithful are warriors and guards who defend their people with courage.

Dogma

The safety of the people comes first. Keep watch, defend your own and be ready to fight.

The faithful

Gaerdal's faithful are serious, vigilant and protective. They defend their community, stand guard and train for combat. They are more solemn than most gnomes and often wear an iron band as a sign of devotion. They believe the safety of the people comes first. Their rites include oaths of protection and defence drills.

Garl Glittergold

God of trickery and gems

Overview

TitleGod of trickery and gems
EpithetsThe Joker, The Sparkling One
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA gold nugget
Home planeBytopia (Golden Hills)
Typical worshippersGnomes, pranksters, jewellers

Description

Garl Glittergold is the head of the gnomish pantheon, the Lords of the Golden Hills. He is the god of humour, pranks, gems and protection. Cheerful and mischievous, he loves playing tricks, but protects his people fiercely. He is the sworn enemy of Kurtulmak, the god of kobolds.

Dogma

Laughter is the best weapon. Play tricks, protect your people and appreciate the beauty of gems.

The faithful

Garl's faithful are cheerful, mischievous and fiercely protective. They tell jokes, play tricks and throw parties full of humour, but become formidable when their community is threatened. They love gems, goldsmithing and ingenious mechanisms. They believe laughter is the best weapon against despair and that wit is worth more than strength. Their rites include prank contests, recitals and offerings of gold nuggets.

Gond

God of craft

Overview

TitleGod of craft
EpithetsThe Holy Maker of All Things, The Inspiration Divine, Wonderbringer
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsForge, Knowledge
SymbolA toothed cog with four spokes
Home planeThe Outlands
Typical worshippersArtificers, artisans, engineers, inventors

Description

Gond is the god of invention, machines and know-how. He loves novelty and rewards those who dare to experiment, even if their creations sometimes explode. His greatest centre of worship is in Lantan, an island where his priests have perfected extraordinary mechanisms. His faithful travel from town to town to share inventions and techniques, and see every well-designed tool as a prayer to their god.

Dogma

Creating is the highest calling. Invent, experiment, perfect and spread new techniques so that the world progresses.

The faithful

Gond's faithful always have their hands busy. They take apart, improve and reinvent everything that comes to hand, and consider that a failed invention is still an offering. They travel to share techniques and plans, and mark their creations with a small cog. Their temples look like noisy workshops, full of gears, furnaces and prototypes. They are curious, pragmatic and sometimes reckless, ready to test a dangerous invention “just to see”. They hate stagnation and people who say “we've always done it this way”.

Gorm Gulthyn

God of vigilance

Overview

TitleGod of vigilance
EpithetsThe Guardian of All Dwarves, The Lord of the Bronze Mask
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolA bronze half-mask
Home planeMount Celestia
Typical worshippersDwarven guards, sentinels, defenders

Description

Gorm Gulthyn is the dwarven god of protection and vigilance. Always depicted wearing a bronze mask, he stands guard at the gates of dwarven fortresses. His faithful are sentinels and defenders, ready to sacrifice their lives to protect their clan. He never sleeps and never lowers his guard.

Dogma

Vigilance is the price of safety. Guard the gates, defend the clan and never let your attention slip.

The faithful

Gorm's faithful are serious, unbending guardians. They take their watch as a sacred duty, check every corner of the walls and never lower their guard. Many wear a bronze half-mask as a sign of devotion. They believe the safety of the clan comes before their own comfort and even before their lives. They despise traitors and careless sentinels, whom they punish severely. Their rites are guard vigils held in silence, standing, before the gates of the fortress.

Grumbar

God of earth

Overview

TitleGod of earth
EpithetsThe Lord of the Earth, The King Under the Mountain
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsKnowledge
SymbolA mountain
Home planeElemental Plane of Earth
Typical worshippersMiners, earth genasi, settled folk

Description

Grumbar is the elemental power of earth: rock, mountain, the stable ground beneath one's feet. Slow, unchanging and almost indifferent to mortals, he represents permanence and resistance to change. He is Akadi's natural opposite. Those who dig, build foundations or seek stability in a restless world address their prayers to him.

Dogma

What is solid endures. Resist needless change, build to last and respect the weight of old things.

The faithful

Grumbar's faithful are slow to decide and almost impossible to change their minds. They value stability, tradition and good work that lasts for centuries. They are found among miners, masons and keepers of old houses. They pray by laying their hands on bare rock and bury their offerings rather than burn them. Their few temples are carved into the mountain. They distrust fashions, travellers and new ideas, and prefer proven solutions.

Gruumsh

God of storms and war

Overview

TitleGod of storms and war
EpithetsHe Who Watches, One-Eye
PantheonOrc pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsTempest, War
SymbolAn unblinking eye
Home planeAcheron (Nishrek)
Typical worshippersOrcs, orc warriors, horde leaders

Description

Gruumsh is the head of the orc pantheon and the god of war, conquest and storms. He is said to have lost an eye fighting Corellon, and has nursed an eternal hatred of elves ever since. He drives orcs to conquer and destroy. His faithful are fearsome warriors.

Dogma

The orcs must conquer the world. Fight, destroy the elves and take what rightfully belongs to the orc people.

The faithful

Gruumsh's faithful are violent, conquering orc warriors. They believe orcs must dominate the world and that elves are their eternal enemies. Some priests put out one of their eyes in homage to their one-eyed god. They organise raids, loot villages and sacrifice their prisoners. Their rites include war chants and bloody sacrifices.

Gwaeron Windstrom

God of tracking

Overview

TitleGod of tracking
EpithetsThe Mouth of Mielikki, The Master Tracker, The Tracker Who Never Goes Astray
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsKnowledge, Nature
SymbolA paw print with a five-pointed star at its centre
Home planeThe Beastlands
Typical worshippersRangers, trackers, nature-respecting hunters

Description

Gwaeron Windstrom is a lesser god in the service of Mielikki, for whom he speaks to the rangers of the North. Patron of trackers, he is said never to lose a trail, and scouts call on him before following a difficult track. His most famous holy site is near Triboar, where a stone is said to mark the place where he appeared to mortals.

Dogma

Every creature leaves a trail for those who know how to look. Learn to read nature, protect the wild lands and teach the art of tracking.

The faithful

Gwaeron's faithful are born observers. They read the ground as others read a book, and spend their time teaching the art of tracking to young rangers. They are discreet, patient and respectful of game. They sometimes gather around Gwaeron's Stone near Triboar. Their thinking is simple: everything leaves a trace, and whoever can read them never gets lost. They work closely with Mielikki's faithful and hunt down those who track for pleasure.

Haela Brightaxe

Goddess of luck in battle

Overview

TitleGoddess of luck in battle
EpithetsThe Lady of the Axe, The Joy of Battle
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolAn upright sword whose blade is wrapped in a spiral of flame
Home planeYsgard
Typical worshippersDwarven warriors, adventurers, monster hunters

Description

Haela is the dwarven goddess of luck in battle and the joy of combat. Cheerful and reckless, she encourages dwarves to fight monsters and seek adventure. She is very popular among dwarven adventurers, who call on her before difficult fights. Her faithful love challenges and laugh in the face of danger.

Dogma

Battle is a joy. Face monsters with courage, seek adventure and trust in luck in battle.

The faithful

Haela's faithful are cheerful, reckless and always ready to fight. They seek out monsters to slay, volunteer for dangerous missions and laugh in the face of danger. They believe combat is a celebration and that luck favours the brave. Many are adventurers or monster hunters, and readily share their loot. Before battle, they call on the goddess by raising their weapon; after a victory, they hold noisy banquets where the day's deeds are recounted. They have little patience for the excessive caution of the elders.

Hanali Celanil

Goddess of love and beauty

Overview

TitleGoddess of love and beauty
EpithetsThe Heart of Gold, The Lady of Love
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsLife
SymbolA golden heart
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersElven lovers, artists, aesthetes

Description

Hanali Celanil is the elven goddess of love, beauty and art. She embodies romantic love and eternal beauty. She is revered by elven lovers and artists. She is renowned for her grace and beauty, and enjoys the company of the other gods.

Dogma

Beauty and love are eternal. Cultivate beauty, love sincerely and create works of art.

The faithful

Hanali's faithful are romantics, artists and lovers of beauty. They celebrate love, create works of art and hold refined festivities. They help couples find each other and console broken hearts. They believe beauty and love are eternal and give meaning to the long lives of elves. Their rites include love songs and offerings of flowers and golden jewellery, often by a fountain.

Helm

God of protection and vigilance

Overview

TitleGod of protection and vigilance
EpithetsHe of the Unsleeping Eyes, The Vigilant One, The Watcher
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsLife, Light, Twilight
SymbolA staring eye on an upright left gauntlet
Home planeMechanus
Typical worshippersExplorers, fighters, guards, paladins

Description

Helm is the guardian par excellence: impassive, loyal and always alert. He protects those entrusted to him, without judging and without faltering. During the Time of Troubles, he obeyed the order to prevent the gods from returning to their planes, even if it meant killing Mystra herself, which still earns him an ambivalent reputation today. His priests and paladins serve as bodyguards, caravan protectors and sentinels.

Dogma

The duty of protection comes first. Stay vigilant, keep your guard commitments and never abandon those you have sworn to defend.

The faithful

Helm's faithful are vigilant, serious and reliable. They rise before others, check the locks twice and never leave a guard post without being relieved. Many serve as caravan guards, temple protectors or bodyguards, and consider their contract sacred. Their prayers are often said in vigil, standing, eyes open. They are sometimes seen as rigid or too obedient, because they carry out a legitimate order even when they dislike it. They hate traitors and sleeping sentinels.

Hoar

God of revenge and retribution

Overview

TitleGod of revenge and retribution
EpithetsThe Doombringer, The Poet of Justice
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolA coin stamped with a two-faced head
Home planeAcheron
Typical worshippersVictims seeking redress, vigilantes, avengers

Description

Hoar is the power of just retribution: he wants every wrong paid back in the same measure, and he savours the poetic irony of a well-chosen punishment. An ancient god from the distant south-east (he was known in Mulhorand as Assuran), he is today mostly worshipped in the regions of the Inner Sea. His faithful are not blind vigilantes: vengeance must be proportionate and strike the true culprit.

Dogma

Every injustice calls for an equal response. Vengeance must be fair, proportionate and, if possible, bear the ironic mark of the wrong it punishes.

The faithful

Hoar's faithful are driven by a keen sense of injustice. They never forget a wrong suffered and wait patiently for the moment to pay it back in kind, ironically if possible. They keep lists of moral debts and sometimes offer to avenge those who lack the means. Their priests act as unofficial legal advisers, helping victims obtain redress. They despise disproportionate vengeance, which creates a new wrong, and leniency, which leaves the culprit unpunished.

Ilmater

God of endurance

Overview

TitleGod of endurance
EpithetsThe Crying God, The One Who Endures, The Broken God
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsLife, Twilight
SymbolHands bound at the wrist with a red cord
Home planeBytopia (Shurrock)
Typical worshippersMonks, the oppressed, the poor

Description

Ilmater is the god of those who suffer and those who relieve them. He endures pain in the place of others, and his compassion knows no bounds. His priests tend the sick, feed the hungry and accompany the dying; they are found in hospices, on battlefields and in wretched neighbourhoods. He is one of the most benevolent gods of Faerûn and forms, with Torm and Tyr, the Triad of justice and good.

Dogma

Suffering can have meaning if it relieves others. Help those who suffer, take their burden upon yourself and never abandon the oppressed.

The faithful

Ilmater's faithful are humble, compassionate and tireless. They tend the sick, feed the hungry, accompany the dying and care for the forgotten. They run hospices, orphanages and soup kitchens, often with very little means. They accept suffering for themselves if it relieves someone else, and some monks voluntarily take the place of a prisoner or a condemned person. They despise no one, not even their enemies, and believe no one should suffer alone.

Ilneval

God of strategy and hordes

Overview

TitleGod of strategy and hordes
EpithetsThe Warlord, The Lieutenant of Gruumsh
PantheonOrc pantheon
AlignmentLawful Evil (LE)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolAn upright blood-spattered sword
Home planeAcheron (Nishrek)
Typical worshippersOrc warlords, strategists

Description

Ilneval is the orc god of strategy, war and command. Gruumsh's lieutenant, he leads the orc hordes into battle. His faithful are warlords who plan attacks.

Dogma

Victory belongs to the most cunning leader. Command, plan and conquer.

The faithful

Ilneval's faithful are cunning and ambitious orc warlords. They plan attacks, lead hordes and seek to take command. They believe victory belongs to the most cunning leader. Their rites take place before battles, with blood-covered swords.

Istishia

God of water

Overview

TitleGod of water
EpithetsThe King of Water Beings, The Water Lord
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsTempest
SymbolA wave
Home planeElemental Plane of Water
Typical worshippersSailors, fishers, water genasi

Description

Istishia is the elemental power of water, with its two faces: calm and nurturing, or raging and engulfing. Like the other elemental lords, he takes little interest in mortals and has only a handful of priests. He opposes Kossuth, fire. Seafarers often prefer to pray to Valkur or appease Umberlee, but Istishia is honoured by those who see water as a philosophical principle of adaptation.

Dogma

Water takes every shape and eventually wears down stone. Adapt, persevere and accept that everything flows and changes.

The faithful

Istishia's faithful are flexible, patient and detached from material goods. They believe that everything changes in the end and that it is better to follow the current than to fight it; in conflict, they give ground so as to flow around the obstacle. Fishers and sailors pray to him before setting sail and pour a little fresh water into the sea as an offering. His few priests are wandering philosophers who teach through parables (water wearing down stone, the river that always finds the sea) and who purify wells and springs. They distrust the faithful of Kossuth and all who want to freeze the world in place.

Jergal

Scribe of the dead

Overview

TitleScribe of the dead
EpithetsThe Final Scribe, The Pitiless One, The Bleak Seneschal
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsKnowledge, Death
SymbolA skull biting a scroll
Home planeFugue Plane
Typical worshippersFuneral archivists, obituarists, keepers of the dead

Description

Jergal was once the lord of the end of all things: death, murder and tyranny. Weary of that power, he gave it up to the three mortals who would become Bane, Bhaal and Myrkul, and has since been content to serve. Today he keeps the records of every soul that arrives in the Fugue Plane and assists Kelemvor. Few pray to him, but those who record deaths and inheritances respect him.

Dogma

Every existence has an end and deserves to be recorded. Keep exact records, respect the dead and accept the order of things without passion.

The faithful

Jergal's faithful are cold, precise and dispassionate. They keep death registers, draft wills and make sure every death is properly recorded. They do not fear death and speak of it with a detachment that unsettles the living. They are often embalmers, funeral archivists or notaries. Their rites are sober: reading the names of the departed, sealing the registers. They scorn ambition, which they consider vain since everything ends up in the same ledger.

Kelemvor

God of the dead

Overview

TitleGod of the dead
EpithetsThe Judge of the Damned, The Lord of the Dead
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsDeath, Grave
SymbolAn upright skeletal arm holding balanced scales
Home planeAstral Plane (Fugue Plane)
Typical worshippersFuneral workers, the dying

Description

A former mortal adventurer, Kelemvor succeeded Cyric as ruler of the realm of the dead. He judges souls fairly and sends them to the deity they served, or to the Wall of the Faithless for those who honoured no god. He wants death to be seen as a natural step, neither feared nor sought. His priests organise funerals, comfort the bereaved and hunt the undead, who are an insult to the natural order.

Dogma

Death is part of life and should not be feared. Honour the dead, accompany the dying and destroy the undead who refuse their end.

The faithful

Kelemvor's faithful have a peaceful relationship with death. They organise funerals, comfort the bereaved and accompany the dying so that they may pass without fear. They teach that death is just and that everyone will receive what they deserve. They loathe the undead, whom they hunt relentlessly, and distrust necromancers. They refuse to prolong life artificially beyond what is reasonable. Their temples are sober, with memorial gardens and carefully tended cemeteries.

Kiaransalee

Goddess of necromancy

Overview

TitleGoddess of necromancy
EpithetsThe Lady of the Dead, The Revenancer
PantheonDrow pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsArcana
SymbolA drow hand wearing many silver rings
Home planeThe Abyss (Thanatos)
Typical worshippersDrow necromancers, undead

Description

Kiaransalee is the drow goddess of the undead and of vengeance. A former drow queen turned goddess, she rules a layer of the Abyss populated by undead. She is the enemy of Lolth, who destroyed one of her temples. Her faithful are necromancers who want to bend the living to their will.

Dogma

The dead must serve the living, and the living the dead. Master necromancy, take vengeance on your enemies and never forgive.

The faithful

Kiaransalee's faithful are drow necromancers obsessed with vengeance and mastery over the dead. They animate corpses, desecrate tombs and turn their enemies into undead servants. They wear many silver rings, symbols of their goddess. They hate the faithful of Lolth and seek to destroy them. Their rites take place in crypts and consist of raising the dead in macabre ceremonies. They believe the dead must serve, and that vengeance must never be forgotten.

Kossuth

God of fire

Overview

TitleGod of fire
EpithetsThe Lord of Flames, The Eternal Flame
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsLight
SymbolA flame
Home planeElemental Plane of Fire
Typical worshippersSmiths, fire genasi, followers of purification

Description

Kossuth is the elemental lord of fire, the force that purifies and transforms. Unlike the other elemental powers, he has a fairly structured church, notably in Thay, where his temples are influential. His faithful see fire as both a trial and a rebirth: whatever passes through the flames comes out purer. He is the adversary of Istishia.

Dogma

Fire purifies everything. Perfect yourself through trials, climb the hierarchy by merit and transform the world as flame transforms matter.

The faithful

Kossuth's faithful believe in self-improvement through trials. They hold rituals of firewalking, fasting and purification by heat. Their church is very hierarchical: one rises in rank by merit, often proven through ordeals. They tend sacred fires that must never go out. They are ambitious, determined and sometimes arrogant toward those who refuse to surpass themselves. In Thay, they play an important political and commercial role.

Labelas Enoreth

God of time, history and philosophy

Overview

TitleGod of time, history and philosophy
EpithetsThe Lord of the Continuum, The Giver of Life
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsArcana, Knowledge
SymbolA setting sun
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersHistorians, philosophers, elven sages

Description

Labelas Enoreth is the elven god of time, longevity, history and philosophy. He is said to have given the elves their long lives. His faithful are historians, sages and philosophers who preserve the memory of the elven people. He is depicted with a single eye, which he is said to have lost fighting Gruumsh.

Dogma

Time is a gift to be used wisely. Study history, meditate and pass wisdom on to future generations.

The faithful

Labelas's faithful are wise, patient and thoughtful. They study history, meditate on the passage of time and preserve the memory of the elven people in vast archives. They advise rulers by reminding them of past mistakes. They believe the long life of the elves is a gift to be used wisely, not wasted. Their rites take place at sunset, a moment to reflect on the day gone by.

Laduguer

Duergar god of magic and slavery

Overview

TitleDuergar god of magic and slavery
EpithetsThe Gray Protector, The Master of Chains
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentLawful Evil (LE)
Suggested domainsArcana, Death
SymbolA broken arrow
Home planeAcheron
Typical worshippersDuergar, artisans, slavers

Description

Laduguer is the chief god of the duergar, the gray dwarves of the Underdark. He embodies hard work, discipline and resentment toward the other dwarven gods, whom he accuses of abandoning his people. He preaches self-sufficiency, craftsmanship and domination of other races through slavery. His faithful are austere and suspicious.

Dogma

Work is the only truth. Toil without rest, rely only on yourself and subjugate other races to serve the duergar people.

The faithful

Laduguer's faithful are austere duergar, hard-working and suspicious of everyone. They believe the other dwarven gods abandoned their people and that only work and discipline allow survival. They work to exhaustion, live without comfort and regard joy as weakness. They practise slavery and see other races as labour. Their rites are sober: prayers repeated during work, oaths of loyalty to the clan. They hate surface dwarves, whom they see as traitors.

Lathander

God of dawn and renewal

Overview

TitleGod of dawn and renewal
EpithetsThe Morninglord, The Inspiration Dawn, The Rose-and-Gold God
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsLife, Light
SymbolA road travelling into a sunrise
Home planeElysium (Eronia)
Typical worshippersAristocrats, athletes, merchants, the young

Description

Lathander is the god of dawn and of everything that begins: spring, birth, youth, creativity, new ventures. Optimistic and sometimes excessive, he embodies the idea that each day offers a new chance. People pray to him before a journey or an undertaking, and his priests celebrate weddings and births. His temples are rich and readily ostentatious, covered in stained glass and works of art. His faithful hate the undead, who cling to the past instead of being reborn.

Dogma

Every morning is a new beginning. Cultivate hope, encourage creation and renewal, and destroy the undead who deny the cycle of life.

The faithful

Lathander's faithful are optimistic, energetic and sometimes exuberant. They rise at dawn to greet the sun with songs, encourage new projects and readily lend money to those who want to start a business. They love colourful clothing, art and great festivals. They celebrate births, weddings and beginnings of every kind. They believe no one is lost and that everyone can change. They do, however, hate the undead, whom they hunt relentlessly.

Leira

Goddess of illusion

Overview

TitleGoddess of illusion
EpithetsThe Lady of Deception, The Lady of the Mists, Mistshadow
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Neutral (CN)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA point-down triangle containing a swirl of mist
Home planeLimbo
Typical worshippersActors, swindlers, illusionists, rogues

Description

Leira is the goddess of illusion and deception, but also of imagination. She is neither benevolent nor malevolent: she simply reminds us that appearances deceive. She was said to have perished during the Time of Troubles, but her cult has resurfaced. Her faithful, always veiled, refuse to tell the whole truth and distrust those who claim to hold it.

Dogma

Nothing is quite what it seems. Doubt certainties, master the art of illusion and never let yourself be locked into a single truth.

The faithful

Leira's faithful often wear a veil or a mask of mist, and never tell the whole truth, not even to those close to them. They believe reality is just one illusion among others and that certainties make people dangerous; so they like to sow doubt among fanatics. They are found among actors, illusionists, spies and swindlers. Their ceremonies are performances where no one knows which part is real, and their temples are hidden behind false façades. They distrust the priests of Savras and Tyr, and consider that a well-woven lie can be a work of art, or a protection.

Lliira

Goddess of joy

Overview

TitleGoddess of joy
EpithetsThe Mistress of Revels, Our Lady of Joy
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsLife
SymbolA triangle of three six-pointed stars
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersBards, dancers, poets, revellers, singers

Description

Lliira is the goddess of joy, dance and celebration. She presides over festivals, celebrations and moments of freedom when worries are forgotten. She hates violence so much that her faithful never shed blood in her temples. Close to Sune and Milil, she is especially popular in Waterdeep and in the festive cities of the Sword Coast.

Dogma

Joy is a gift to be shared. Celebrate life, hold festivals open to all and bring a little happiness to those who lack it.

The faithful

Lliira's faithful are joyful, sociable and generous. They organise parties, balls and festivals open to all, and consider a successful celebration the finest of prayers. They allow no weapons in their temples and prefer to defuse a brawl with a song or a dance; shedding blood during a festival is sacrilege to them. They visit the bereaved to remind them that joy will return, and fund festivals in poor districts. They are sometimes accused of frivolity, but they sincerely believe that joy protects against despair and that it is contagious.

Lolth

Goddess of spiders

Overview

TitleGoddess of spiders
EpithetsThe Spider Queen, The Queen of the Demonweb Pits
PantheonDrow pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA spider
Home planeThe Abyss (Demonweb Pits)
Typical worshippersEvil drow, Underdark travellers

Description

Lolth is the goddess of the drow, of spiders and of chaos. She rules drow society through her priestesses, who govern the great cities of the Underdark such as Menzoberranzan. She encourages intrigue, betrayal and cruelty, constantly testing her faithful. She was once Araushnee, an elven goddess, before being banished for betraying Corellon.

Dogma

Only the strongest and most ruthless deserve to rule. Serve Lolth without fail, crush your rivals and maintain the supremacy of the priestesses.

The faithful

Lolth's faithful live in a world of intrigue, betrayal and cruelty. The priestesses rule drow society and the noble houses compete for the goddess's favour. They believe only the strongest and most ruthless deserve to rule. They practise sacrifices, bloody rituals and ordeals to prove their worth. Males are relegated to subordinate roles. They despise other races and the drow who flee to the surface.

Loviatar

Goddess of pain

Overview

TitleGoddess of pain
EpithetsThe Maiden of Pain, The Mistress of the Whip, The Willing Whip
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Evil (LE)
Suggested domainsDeath
SymbolA nine-tailed barbed scourge
Home planeGehenna (Mungoth)
Typical worshippersPeople suffering pain or betrayal

Description

Loviatar is the goddess of suffering, which she considers a path to strength. Cold and cruel, she teaches that pain hardens and that pity is weakness. She serves Bane and stands radically opposed to Ilmater, who relieves the suffering she seeks to inflict. Her priests practise mortification and torture, convinced that pain reveals everyone's truth.

Dogma

Pain makes you strong. Endure, inflict suffering on those who must learn, and never give in to pity.

The faithful

Loviatar's faithful practise suffering as a spiritual discipline. They flagellate themselves, endure hunger and cold, and see each pain as a lesson that hardens the soul. They readily inflict suffering on others on the pretext of educating them, and serve jailers, executioners and tyrants. Their rites include nine lashes, endurance trials and mock tenderness followed by betrayal, for the goddess teaches that the sharpest pain comes from those we love. They deeply despise the faithful of Ilmater and the compassion they consider naive.

Luthic

Mother goddess of fertility and healing

Overview

TitleMother goddess of fertility and healing
EpithetsThe Cave Mother, The Mother of All Orcs
PantheonOrc pantheon
AlignmentLawful Evil (LE)
Suggested domainsLife, Nature
SymbolAn orcish rune meaning 'cave entrance'
Home planeAcheron (Nishrek)
Typical worshippersOrcs, healers, mothers

Description

Luthic is the orc goddess of fertility, healing and caves. Wife of Gruumsh, she protects orc homes and tends the wounded. Her faithful are healers and mothers who watch over the tribe.

Dogma

The tribe must survive and multiply. Protect the home, tend the warriors and defend the caves.

The faithful

Luthic's faithful are orc healers and mothers. They protect homes, tend the wounded and defend the tribe's caves. They believe the tribe must survive and multiply. They let their nails grow like claws in homage to their goddess. Their rites take place in caves.

Malar

God of the hunt

Overview

TitleGod of the hunt
EpithetsThe Beastlord, The Blood God, The Wild Hunter
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsNature
SymbolA clawed paw
Home planeCarceri (Colothys)
Typical worshippersBarbarians, hunters, lycanthropes

Description

Malar is nature at its bloodiest: the stalk, the predator's instinct, the kill. He is worshipped by hunters who hunt for the pleasure of killing, by some barbarians and by many lycanthropes. His faithful organise ritual hunts, sometimes of human prey. He is the sworn enemy of Mielikki and Nobanion, and serves Talos among the Gods of Fury.

Dogma

Life is a hunt. Only the strongest predator deserves to survive; stalk, kill and respect the blood that is shed.

The faithful

Malar's faithful live for the hunt. To them the world is divided into predators and prey, and the only true test of a being is its ability to hunt and kill. They organise great ritual hunts, notably the High Hunt, where the prey is sometimes an intelligent creature or a captured human. They wear trophies from their victims, eat the raw meat of their kills and despise peasants, herders and city folk. Many are lycanthropes and consider their curse a blessing. They are sworn enemies of Mielikki's faithful and of the druids who protect game.

Marthammor Duin

God of travellers

Overview

TitleGod of travellers
EpithetsThe Finder-of-Trails, The Watcher over Wanderers
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsNature, Trickery
SymbolA mace raised before a tall boot
Home planeThe Outlands
Typical worshippersTravelling dwarves, explorers, itinerant merchants

Description

Marthammor Duin is the god of dwarves who travel far from their stronghold. He protects explorers, itinerant merchants and dwarves who live among other peoples. He is also the god of lightning and of lost travellers. His faithful help travellers and maintain relations between dwarves and other races.

Dogma

The world is vast and deserves to be explored. Help travellers, forge bonds with other peoples and never forget your roots.

The faithful

Marthammor's faithful are travelling dwarves, open-minded and curious about the world. They explore far from their stronghold, trade with other peoples and often serve as go-betweens for dwarves and humans. They carve signs along the roads to guide travellers and help isolated dwarves. They believe the world is vast and that one can stay true to one's roots while roaming it. Their rites are simple and performed on the road, often around a campfire, while sharing travel stories.

Mask

God of thieves

Overview

TitleGod of thieves
EpithetsThe Lord of Shadows, The Master of All Thieves
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Neutral (CN)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA black mask
Home planeHades (Niflheim)
Typical worshippersAssassins, rogues, thieves, tricksters

Description

Mask is the god of thieves, shadows and intrigue. He values subtlety over violence and delights in elaborate schemes. He has lost and regained his powers several times, notably against Cyric and Shar, which makes him both cunning and vindictive. Thieves' guilds honour him discreetly and set aside a share of every haul for him.

Dogma

Everything belongs to whoever knows how to take it. Act in the shadows, prefer cunning to force and never get caught.

The faithful

Mask's faithful are discreet, cunning and patient. They prefer an elaborate plan to brute force, and consider a perfect theft, with no witness and no violence, the finest prayer one can offer. They meet in temples hidden behind a shop, a tavern or a gambling house, and give their god a share of every haul. They hate needless violence, which draws the watch, and despise clumsy thieves. They believe everything belongs to whoever knows how to take it, that naive honesty is a weakness and that secrets are worth more than gold.

Mielikki

Goddess of forests

Overview

TitleGoddess of forests
EpithetsOur Lady of the Forest, The Forest Queen
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsNature
SymbolA unicorn's head
Home planeThe Beastlands (Krigala)
Typical worshippersFey, foresters, rangers

Description

Mielikki is the goddess of forests and their inhabitants. She embodies the balance between people and nature: one may live from the forest, provided one respects it. Patron of rangers, dryads and unicorns, she is the daughter of Silvanus. Her cult is strong in the North, notably around the High Forest. The famous Drizzt Do'Urden is one of her best-known faithful.

Dogma

The forest feeds those who respect it. Protect the woods and their creatures, live in harmony with them and guide those who venture there.

The faithful

Mielikki's faithful live to the rhythm of the forest. They hunt out of necessity and always with respect, cut only the trees they need and replant what they take. They guide lost travellers, tend wounded animals and defend the woods against greedy loggers as well as cruel hunters. Many are rangers, foresters or druids, and they hold their rites in clearings, under the moon, around an ancient tree. They believe people can live from nature without destroying it and are kindly toward fey, dryads and unicorns.

Milil

God of poetry and song

Overview

TitleGod of poetry and song
EpithetsThe Lord of All Songs, The First Poet, Oghma's Bard
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsLight
SymbolA five-stringed harp made of leaves
Home planeElysium (Amoria)
Typical worshippersBards, orators, poets, singers

Description

Milil is the god of music, poetry and eloquence. A servant of Oghma, he watches over inspiration and the art of composition. His faithful are bards, orators and singers, but also music teachers. His temples are often concert halls with remarkable acoustics. He is a little vain and likes his creations to be praised.

Dogma

Music and speech lift the soul. Create, perform with talent, pass on the old songs and encourage young artists.

The faithful

Milil's faithful are passionate artists. They sing, compose, recite poems and learn the old ballads by heart so that they are not lost. Their temples are halls with remarkable acoustics where singing contests, poetry jousts and free concerts are held. They encourage young talent and teach music to children.
