They believe music and speech can change people's hearts and calm a crowd. Like their god, they are sometimes vain and sensitive to compliments, and cannot bear having a song interrupted.

Moradin

God of creation

Overview

TitleGod of creation
EpithetsThe Soul Forger, The Dwarffather, The All-Father
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsForge, Knowledge
SymbolA hammer and anvil
Home planeMount Celestia (Erackinor)
Typical worshippersDwarves, smiths, artisans, clan leaders

Description

Moradin is the father and creator of the dwarves: legend says he forged their souls in the fire of his divine forge, from metal and precious stone. Head of the dwarven pantheon (the Morndinsamman), he embodies craftsmanship, tradition, family and the protection of the clan. Stern but fair, he judges dwarves by the quality of their work and their loyalty to their own. Almost every dwarven home has a small altar to him near the forge.

Dogma

Work well done honours the ancestors. Forge with care, protect the clan, respect traditions and pass your skills on to the next generations.

The faithful

Moradin's faithful are proud, hard-working and deeply attached to tradition. To them, work well done is a prayer and a botched object a shame for the whole clan. Every home has a small altar near the forge, where an apprentice's first successful piece is laid. Priests serve as judges, arbiters between clans and keepers of the lineages; they bless new forges and the foundations of halls. The faithful believe honour is measured by loyalty to the clan and by the quality of what one leaves behind. They distrust changes that come too fast, easy promises and outsiders who do not respect custom.

Myrkul

God of death

Overview

TitleGod of death
EpithetsThe Lord of Bones, Old Lord Skull, The Reaper
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Evil (NE)
Suggested domainsDeath
SymbolA white human skull
Home planeHades (Oinos)
Typical worshippersNecromancers, undead

Description

Myrkul, a member of the Dead Three, is the god of death in its most sinister aspect: decay, exhaustion, the fear of the end. He once ruled the dead before perishing during the Time of Troubles, then returned in a different form. Necromancers worship him for his control over the undead, and his cults seek to spread the fear of death rather than death itself.

Dogma

Death is inevitable and everyone ends up belonging to it. Fear it, serve it and use its power to enslave the living and the dead alike.

The faithful

Myrkul's faithful are grim, cold and fatalistic. They see the living as future servants and the fear of death as an instrument of power. They practise necromancy, animate corpses and maintain secret crypts, often beneath cemeteries or abandoned temples. They spread frightening rumours, desecrate tombs and seek to make people doubt any peaceful rest after death. Their rites take place at night, among bones, with deep chants and offerings of skulls. They hate the faithful of Kelemvor, whom they accuse of usurping their god's throne.

Mystra

Goddess of magic

Overview

TitleGoddess of magic
EpithetsThe Lady of Mysteries, The Mother of All Magic, Our Lady of Spells
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsArcana, Knowledge
SymbolA circle of seven stars, nine stars encircling a red mist, or a single star
Home planeElysium (Eronia)
Typical worshippersAll who use magic

Description

Mystra is the guardian of the Weave, the magical fabric that allows mortals to cast spells. She is one of the most important deities of Faerûn: when she disappeared, magic itself collapsed, causing the Spellplague. Several women have borne her name over the ages, the goddess being reborn after each death. She chooses mortal Chosen, such as Elminster, to watch over magic and keep it out of the wrong hands.

Dogma

Magic is a gift that demands responsibility. Use it wisely, protect it from those who abuse it and preserve the Weave.

The faithful

Mystra's faithful feel a mixture of respect and wonder toward magic. They study it rigorously, protect the places where the Weave is fragile, preserve ancient spellbooks and keep watch on those who abuse magic. They believe magical power carries a responsibility toward others, and some of them hunt down mages who seek to dominate through magic. Their rites include demonstrations of spells, vigils under the stars and prayers for the balance of the Weave. They keep a painful memory of the Spellplague, which reminds them how precious and fragile magic is.

Nebelun

God of invention and luck

Overview

TitleGod of invention and luck
EpithetsThe Meddler, The Tinkerer
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsKnowledge, Trickery
SymbolA bellows and a lizard's tail
Home planeBytopia (Golden Hills)
Typical worshippersGnome inventors, tinkerers, experimenters

Description

Nebelun is the gnome god of invention, curiosity and luck. He urges gnomes to experiment, even if their inventions sometimes explode. Some sages consider him an aspect of Gond. His faithful are tinkerers and inventors who love bold experiments.

Dogma

Every experiment is worth trying. Invent, dare and accept that failures lead to the finest discoveries.

The faithful

Nebelun's faithful are bold and curious tinkerers. They invent, experiment and accept that their inventions sometimes explode, which makes them the terror of their neighbours. They believe every experiment is worth trying and that a failure is a lesson. Their rites include demonstrations of inventions, often spectacular and sometimes dangerous.

Oghma

God of knowledge

Overview

TitleGod of knowledge
EpithetsThe Binder of What Is Known, The Lord of Knowledge
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsKnowledge
SymbolA blank scroll
Home planeThe Outlands
Typical worshippersArchivists, cartographers, sages

Description

Oghma is the god of knowledge in all its forms, but above all of ideas: he created concepts before they were written or sung. Deneir and Milil serve him. His priests are scholars, advisers and collectors of knowledge who want ideas to circulate freely. He is worshipped in the libraries and academies of all Faerûn.

Dogma

Knowledge is the greatest wealth. Seek it, preserve it, share it freely and never destroy it.

The faithful

Oghma's faithful are curious, learned and open-minded. They collect books, ideas, languages and legends, and love to debate late into the night. They found libraries, academies and learned societies, and often serve as advisers to rulers. They hold that knowledge must circulate freely, oppose censorship and consider the destruction of a book a crime. Their rites take the form of public debates, recitations and the passing of knowledge from master to pupil. They will sell some knowledge, but never hide it from the world.

Rillifane Rallathil

God of nature

Overview

TitleGod of nature
EpithetsThe Leaflord, The Great Oak
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsNature
SymbolAn oak tree
Home planeArborea
Typical worshippersWood elves, druids, rangers

Description

Rillifane Rallathil is the elven god of nature, forests and druids. He is depicted as an immense oak whose roots touch every wood. He protects forests and their inhabitants, and is especially revered by wood elves. His faithful defend nature against those who destroy it.

Dogma

The forest is the mother of all life. Protect the woods, live in harmony with nature and fight those who threaten it.

The faithful

Rillifane's faithful are protectors of the forest. They live in harmony with the trees and know every path and every creature of the woods. They fight those who fell forests, sometimes with great violence. They believe the forest is the mother of all life and that every tree has a soul. Their rites take place under great ancient oaks, with songs that accompany the rustling of the leaves. Many are druids or rangers.

Savras

God of divination and fate

Overview

TitleGod of divination and fate
EpithetsThe All-Seeing, The Third Eye, The Lord of Divination
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsArcana, Knowledge
SymbolA crystal ball containing many eyes
Home planeArcadia
Typical worshippersDiviners, oracles, judges, truth seekers

Description

Savras is the god of divination, prophecy and truth. He was once imprisoned by Azuth in a staff before reconciling with him; today he serves Mystra. His faithful practise divination and the search for truth, and are often called upon to unmask liars. He is naturally opposed to Cyric.

Dogma

Truth is within reach of those who know how to seek it. Study omens, speak what you see and unmask lies.

The faithful

Savras's faithful seek the truth in omens, dreams, cards and crystal balls. They are diviners, oracles, investigators or advisers, and readily serve judges to unmask liars. They believe the truth always comes out for those who know how to look, and that fate has a shape that can be read. They speak little, observe much and always seem to know more than they say, which often makes them unsettling. They despise Cyric's lies and Leira's illusions.

Segojan Earthcaller

God of earth and the dead

Overview

TitleGod of earth and the dead
EpithetsThe Lord of the Burrow, The Keeper of Graves
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Good (NG)
Suggested domainsLight
SymbolA glowing gemstone
Home planeBytopia (Golden Hills)
Typical worshippersGnomes, druids, keepers of the dead

Description

Segojan Earthcaller is the gnome god of earth, nature and the dead. He protects gnome burrows and guides the souls of the departed. His faithful are druids and guardians who watch over the dead and the earth.

Dogma

The earth is our home and our final resting place. Respect the earth, honour the dead and protect the burrows.

The faithful

Segojan's faithful are close to the earth and respectful of the dead. They protect burrows, honour the departed and watch over underground nature. They believe the earth is both our home and our final resting place. They organise gnome funerals. Their rites take place underground, around glowing gems.

Sehanine Moonbow

Goddess of divination, dreams, journeys and death

Overview

TitleGoddess of divination, dreams, journeys and death
EpithetsThe Daughter of the Night Skies, The Lady of the Moon
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsKnowledge
SymbolA full moon under a moonbow
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersElves, diviners, travellers, the dying

Description

Sehanine Moonbow is the elven goddess of the moon, dreams, mysteries and death. She guides elven souls to Arvandor after death and watches over the dreams of elves. Her faithful are diviners and mystics who seek truth in dreams and visions.

Dogma

Life is a journey of which death is only one stage. Listen to your dreams, seek out mysteries and guide souls to their rest.

The faithful

Sehanine's faithful are mystical, dreamy and contemplative. They study dreams, interpret omens and guide the souls of the dying to Arvandor. They accompany the elves who depart westward at the end of their lives. They believe death is only one stage and that dreams reveal hidden truths. Their rites take place at night, under the moon, with meditations and slow chants.

Selûne

Goddess of the moon

Overview

TitleGoddess of the moon
EpithetsThe Moonmaiden, The Night White Lady, Our Lady of Silver
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsKnowledge, Life, Twilight
SymbolA pair of eyes surrounded by seven stars
Home planeYsgard
Typical worshippersLycanthropes, sailors, spellcasters

Description

Selûne is the goddess of the moon, the starry night, navigation and spells. She was born at the same time as Shar, her twin sister and worst enemy: one is light in the night, the other absolute darkness. Her faithful guide travellers, help good lycanthropes master their curse and fight the cults of Shar. She is especially present in coastal regions and among navigators.

Dogma

Light endures even in the darkest night. Guide those who are lost, protect the outcasts and fight the darkness of Shar.

The faithful

Selûne's faithful are kindly, open-minded and often nocturnal. They guide lost travellers, protect outcasts and help good lycanthropes live with their curse. They celebrate the full moon with dances, songs and open-air prayers, often near water. Many are sailors, navigators or spellcasters, and the faith gives a large place to women. They actively hunt the cults of Shar, which they infiltrate and dismantle. They believe even the darkest night carries a light, and that no one is too lost to be found.

Selvetarm

God of warriors

Overview

TitleGod of warriors
EpithetsThe Champion of Lolth, The Spider That Waits
PantheonDrow pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolA spider above a crossed sword and mace
Home planeThe Abyss
Typical worshippersDrow warriors

Description

Selvetarm is the drow god of warriors and fighters. Champion of Lolth, he has been bound to her will since she defeated him. He is filled with rage and hatred, and his faithful are fearsome warriors who fight for the glory of Lolth.

Dogma

Strength in battle is the only value. Fight with rage, serve Lolth and destroy her enemies.

The faithful

Selvetarm's faithful are fierce, disciplined drow warriors, often full of rage. They train relentlessly and consider combat their only reason for being. They serve Lolth through their god, who is her chained champion. They believe strength in battle is the only value. Their rites include bloody duels and sacrifices offered before battles.

Shar

Goddess of darkness and loss

Overview

TitleGoddess of darkness and loss
EpithetsThe Mistress of the Night, The Dark Lady, Our Lady of Loss
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Evil (NE)
Suggested domainsDeath, Trickery
SymbolA black disk encircled with a border of purple
Home planeHades (Niflheim)
Typical worshippersPeople suffering pain or loss

Description

Shar is the goddess of darkness, oblivion and loss. She seduces wounded souls by promising to erase their pain, at the cost of their past and their identity. She wove the Shadow Weave, a rival to Mystra's Weave, and has caused many catastrophes. Her cult acts in secret, infiltrates institutions and aims to plunge the world into nothingness. She is the twin sister and enemy of Selûne.

Dogma

All things end in oblivion. Accept loss, reveal to others the vanity of hope and prepare for the return of the eternal night.

The faithful

Shar's faithful live in secrecy and infiltration. They recruit people broken by grief, shame or failure, and promise them oblivion from their pain in exchange for their loyalty. They infiltrate councils, guilds and even rival temples, patiently preparing plots that sometimes last for generations. Their rites are held in total darkness, in hidden sanctuaries where vows of oblivion are spoken. They believe everything ends in nothingness, that hope is a cruel illusion and that to remember is to suffer. They hate the faithful of Selûne with rare intensity.

Shargaas

God of stealth and darkness

Overview

TitleGod of stealth and darkness
EpithetsThe Night Lord, The Stalker Below
PantheonOrc pantheon
AlignmentNeutral Evil (NE)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA red crescent moon with a skull between its horns
Home planeAcheron (Nishrek)
Typical worshippersOrc thieves, assassins

Description

Shargaas is the orc god of night, stealth and thieves. He dwells in darkness and favours surprise attacks. His faithful are thieves and assassins who act in the shadows.

Dogma

Darkness is a weapon. Strike from the shadows, steal and kill unseen.

The faithful

Shargaas's faithful are orc thieves and assassins. They act at night, strike from the shadows and raid enemy camps. They often live in dark caves. They believe darkness is a weapon. Their rites take place in total darkness.

Sharindlar

Goddess of healing

Overview

TitleGoddess of healing
EpithetsThe Lady of Life and Mercy, The Shining Dancer
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsLife
SymbolA burning needle
Home planeArborea
Typical worshippersDwarven healers, lovers, dancers

Description

Sharindlar is the dwarven goddess of healing, mercy, love and fertility. She heals the wounded, comforts the bereaved and blesses unions. She is also associated with dance and the moon. Her priests are devoted healers who care for all who need it, even their enemies.

Dogma

Mercy is a strength. Heal the wounded, comfort those who suffer and celebrate love and life.

The faithful

Sharindlar's faithful are compassionate, gentle and devoted to others. They heal the wounded, even those of the enemy side, and comfort the bereaved. They celebrate love, marriage and fertility, and help couples start a family. They believe mercy is a strength, not a weakness. Their rites include dances under the moon and healing ceremonies in which a needle is heated in fire to treat wounds. They are highly respected in the strongholds, even by the toughest warriors.

Shaundakul

God of travel

Overview

TitleGod of travel
EpithetsThe Rider of the Winds, The Helping Hand
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Neutral (CN)
Suggested domainsNature, Tempest
SymbolAn outstretched left hand, a gust of wind
Home planeYsgard
Typical worshippersGuides, explorers, rangers, travellers

Description

Shaundakul is the god of travellers, exploration and wide-open spaces. He guides caravan masters, explorers and scouts, and brings unexpected help to those who are lost. He went through a period of being forgotten before finding his faithful again in the North. His temples are rare: he is honoured instead at crossroads, on mountain passes and at roadside inns.

Dogma

The world is made to be travelled. Travel, explore, help travellers in trouble and share the roads you discover.

The faithful

Shaundakul's faithful are tireless travellers. They guide caravans, open new roads and help travellers in trouble, often asking nothing in return. They raise cairns at crossroads, maintain mountain shelters and leave provisions there for those who will come after them. They are open, generous and curious about foreign customs. They pray at the top of mountain passes, facing the wind. They hate highwaymen and the lords who close roads or extort travellers.

Sheela Peryroyl

Goddess of agriculture and weather

Overview

TitleGoddess of agriculture and weather
EpithetsThe Wildflower, The Lady of the Fields
PantheonHalfling pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsNature, Tempest
SymbolA flower
Home planeBytopia (Green Fields)
Typical worshippersHalfling farmers, gardeners

Description

Sheela Peryroyl is the halfling goddess of agriculture, nature and weather. She blesses harvests and brings rain. Her faithful are farmers and gardeners who celebrate the seasons and the harvests.

Dogma

The land gives to those who tend it. Tend the land, celebrate the seasons and respect nature.

The faithful

Sheela's faithful are farmers close to nature. They tend the land, celebrate the seasons and respect the weather. They hold spring and harvest festivals, with dancing and flowers. They believe the land gives to those who tend it. Their rites take place in the fields.

Shevarash

God of vengeance

Overview

TitleGod of vengeance
EpithetsThe Black Archer, The Avenger
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Neutral (CN)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolA broken arrow above a tear
Home planeArborea
Typical worshippersVengeful elves, archers, drow hunters

Description

Shevarash is the elven god of vengeance, hatred of the drow and loss. He has sworn never to smile until Lolth and her faithful are destroyed. His faithful are archers and hunters who track the drow relentlessly. He is grim and implacable.

Dogma

The betrayal of the drow will never be forgiven. Hunt down Lolth and her servants, and never give up on vengeance.

The faithful

Shevarash's faithful are grim, implacable and driven by vengeance. They swear never to smile as long as Lolth and her faithful exist, and devote their lives to hunting the drow. They are often formidable archers who patrol the ways into the Underdark. They believe the betrayal of the drow can never be forgiven. Their rites include oaths of vengeance sworn over a broken arrow.

Silvanus

God of wild nature

Overview

TitleGod of wild nature
EpithetsOak Father, The Old Oak, Old Father Tree
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsNature
SymbolAn oak leaf
Home planeThe Outlands
Typical worshippersBarbarians, druids, rangers, wood elves

Description

Silvanus is wild nature as a whole, and the guarantor of its balance. He is neither kind nor cruel: he makes sure nothing gains the upper hand, whether the civilisation that clears the land or the forces that destroy. His druids are the guardians of that balance, and they do not hesitate to oppose towns that encroach on the forest. He is the leader of the nature gods, whom he guides with wisdom.

Dogma

Nature must stay in balance. Protect wild places, fight those who destroy them and respect the cycle of life and death.

The faithful

Silvanus's faithful are guardians of balance, not pacifists. They protect wild places against land clearing and spreading towns, but they also fight whatever destroys nature from within, such as an epidemic or an invasive creature. They hold their rites in stone circles or under old oaks, and do not hesitate to sabotage human projects that threaten the forest. They are often druids, rangers or barbarians. They accept death as part of the cycle, which sometimes makes them harsh toward sentimental city folk.

Solonor Thelandira

God of archery

Overview

TitleGod of archery
EpithetsThe Great Archer, The Keeper of the Forest
PantheonElven pantheon (Seldarine)
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolA silver arrow with green fletching
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersElven archers, hunters, rangers

Description

Solonor Thelandira is the elven god of archery, hunting and survival in the forest. He is the finest archer of all the gods. His faithful are archers and hunters who protect the elven forests. He teaches patience, precision and respect for the prey.

Dogma

One well-placed arrow is worth a thousand blows. Be patient, precise and respectful of nature.

The faithful

Solonor's faithful are patient archers and hunters. They train relentlessly, protect the forests and respect the game they hunt. They believe one well-placed arrow is worth a thousand wild blows, and that patience is the greatest of a hunter's virtues. Their rites include archery contests and ritual hunts in which the slain animal is thanked.

Sune

Goddess of love and beauty

Overview

TitleGoddess of love and beauty
EpithetsLady Firehair, The Lady of Love, The Princess of Passion
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsLife, Light
SymbolThe face of a beautiful red-haired woman
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersArtists, hedonists, lovers

Description

Sune is the goddess of love, beauty and passion. She prefers sincere emotions to calculation, and believes true beauty is also found in character. Her temples are places of art and beauty, where couples are celebrated and broken hearts welcomed. She is vain and romantic, and is on good terms with Lliira and Lathander.

Dogma

Love and beauty make the world better. Follow your heart, cultivate beauty in yourself and around you, and never scorn a sincere love.

The faithful

Sune's faithful are passionate, romantic and attentive to their appearance. They celebrate love in all its forms, help couples, arrange weddings and console broken hearts. They organise balls, festivals, beauty contests and art exhibitions, and their temples are decorated with mirrors, flowers and red hangings. They believe beauty makes the world better and that one should follow one's heart, even at the cost of some folly. They are sometimes judged shallow, but they bravely defend those they love and loathe moral ugliness as much as physical ugliness.

Talona

Goddess of poison and disease

Overview

TitleGoddess of poison and disease
EpithetsThe Lady of Poison, The Mistress of Disease, The Plague-Crone
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsDeath
SymbolThree teardrops in a triangle
Home planeCarceri (Cathrys)
Typical worshippersPlague victims

Description

Talona is the goddess of disease, poison and plague. People pray to her mainly to spare a region, a herd or a loved one. Her few priests deliberately spread disease, believing the suffering it causes is a tribute. She is especially feared in overcrowded cities and during epidemics.

Dogma

Disease strikes those who do not fear Talona. Appease her with offerings and spread her power so that all learn to dread her.

The faithful

Talona's faithful are few, often feared and sometimes marked by disease themselves. They see epidemics as divine trials: those who survive are blessed, the others have been judged. They prepare poisons and drugs, poison wells and deliberately spread diseases. They live hidden in poor districts, marshes or ruins. Ordinary people, for their part, pray to Talona to be spared and leave offerings near mass graves during epidemics. Her faithful hate healers, whom they see as thieves stealing from their goddess.

Talos

God of storms

Overview

TitleGod of storms
EpithetsThe Destroyer, The Storm Lord, The Raging One
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsTempest
SymbolThree lightning bolts radiating from a central point
Home planePandemonium (Pandesmos)
Typical worshippersBarbarians, druids, raiders

Description

Talos is pure destruction: the storm, the earthquake, the forest fire. Leader of the Gods of Fury (Auril, Malar and Umberlee), he embodies the blind wrath of nature. People pray to him to spare crops and ships, but his faithful believe destruction is necessary for the world to renew itself. He opposes Chauntea and Silvanus.

Dogma

Life is chaos and destruction. Accept the fury of nature, fear it and spread the terror that Talos inspires.

The faithful

Talos's faithful are violent, unpredictable and fascinated by destruction. They believe the world must be destroyed regularly in order to be reborn, and that civilisation is a fragile illusion. They celebrate storms by dancing under the lightning, start fires and plunder villages. His priests extort offerings by promising to spare crops or ships. Ordinary people pray to him to be spared. His faithful despise farmers, builders and the faithful of Chauntea.

Tempus

God of war

Overview

TitleGod of war
EpithetsThe Foehammer, The Lord of Battles
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolAn upright flaming sword
Home planeLimbo
Typical worshippersWarriors, mercenaries, soldiers

Description

Tempus is the god of war, but not of cruelty: he favours one side or the other as chance dictates, and respects courage in all combatants. He is worshipped by soldiers, mercenaries and warriors of every nation. His priests encourage honour in combat, respect for defeated enemies and preparation for battle. It is said he never takes sides for good.

Dogma

War is inevitable and must be waged with honour. Fight with courage, respect your opponent and never kill an unarmed enemy without reason.

The faithful

Tempus's faithful are proud warriors who live by a martial code of honour. They respect courage, even in their enemies, and despise cowardice. Before a battle they pray, sharpen their weapons and sometimes shed a little blood as an offering. After the fight, they bury the dead of both sides with honour. Their temples serve as training grounds, meeting places for mercenaries and refuges for veterans. They believe war is inevitable but must be waged fairly; killing an unarmed prisoner or poisoning a well is a crime in their eyes.

The Red Knight

Goddess of strategy

Overview

TitleGoddess of strategy
EpithetsThe Crimson General, The Grandmaster of the Lanceboard, The Lady of Strategy
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolA red knight lanceboard piece with stars for eyes
Home planeArcadia (Buxenus)
Typical worshippersFighters, gamers, strategists

Description

The Red Knight is the goddess of strategy, planning and tactics. A servant of Tempus, she is revered by generals, strategists and lovers of board games such as lanceboard. Her faithful prepare every battle meticulously and study military history. She shows that a battle is first won in the mind.

Dogma

Victory belongs to whoever prepares best. Plan, study the opponent and never go into a fight without a strategy.

The faithful

The Red Knight's faithful are meticulous strategists. They study military history, analyse past battles and play strategy games such as lanceboard, which they consider a form of prayer. They prepare every fight carefully, anticipate the enemy's moves and despise disorderly charges. Their temples look like war rooms full of maps and models. Many are officers or military advisers. They believe victory is first won in the mind, and that a good plan saves lives.

Torm

God of courage and self-sacrifice

Overview

TitleGod of courage and self-sacrifice
EpithetsThe Hand of Righteousness, The Loyal Fury, Torm the True
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsWar
SymbolA white right gauntlet
Home planeMount Celestia (Mercuria)
Typical worshippersGuardians, knights, paladins

Description

Torm is the god of duty, loyalty and sacrifice. He sets the example for those who sacrifice themselves for others. His paladins, very numerous, serve as protectors and enforcers of justice. He forms the Triad with Tyr and Ilmater, and is particularly opposed to Bane and Cyric. He died during the Time of Troubles fighting Bane, then returned.

Dogma

Duty and loyalty are the greatest virtues. Protect the weak, obey your rightful superiors and be ready to sacrifice everything for the good.

The faithful

Torm's faithful are loyal, brave and devoted to the point of sacrifice. They protect the weak, obey rightful superiors and keep their oaths even at the cost of their lives. Many are paladins, knights or guards. They hold vigils of arms, swear solemn oaths before a white gauntlet and honour the memory of those who died doing their duty. They believe duty comes before personal comfort. They hate traitors, cowards and those who abuse their authority.

Tymora

Goddess of luck

Overview

TitleGoddess of luck
EpithetsLady Luck, Our Smiling Lady
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA face-up coin
Home planeArborea (Arvandor)
Typical worshippersGamblers, Harpers, merchants, rogues

Description

Tymora is the goddess of good fortune, luck and adventure. She smiles on those who take bold risks, and punishes those who are cowardly or overly cautious. She is very popular among adventurers, who often wear her symbol as a lucky charm. She is the twin sister and rival of Beshaba.

Dogma

Fortune favours the bold. Take risks, dare to adventure and do not let fear dictate your choices.

The faithful

Tymora's faithful are bold, optimistic and adventurous. They take risks, play games of chance and readily set off on adventures. They wear her symbol as a lucky charm and flip a coin before big decisions. Her temples heal wounded adventurers and sometimes fund expeditions. They believe fortune favours the bold and that fear is the real enemy. They despise cowardice, but also cheats, who insult luck.

Tyr

God of justice

Overview

TitleGod of justice
EpithetsThe Even-Handed, Grimjaws, The Maimed God
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsWar, Order
SymbolBalanced scales resting on a warhammer
Home planeMount Celestia (Lunia)
Typical worshippersJudges, lawkeepers, lawyers, paladins

Description

Tyr is the god of justice and law. Blind and one-handed since he fought the forces of evil, he embodies impartial, stern justice. He is the head of the Triad, with Torm and Ilmater. His priests are judges, investigators and lawyers; his paladins hunt down criminals. He is worshipped in cities where the law is respected.

Dogma

Justice must be impartial and apply to all. Defend the law, punish the guilty and protect the innocent.

The faithful

Tyr's faithful are just, upright and sometimes uncompromising. They defend the law, investigate crimes and protect the innocent. Many are judges, lawyers, investigators or paladins, and their temples often serve as courts. They believe justice must be impartial and apply to all, rich and poor alike. They swear oaths with a hand on a set of scales and consider perjury a serious crime. They hate criminals, corrupt judges and those who place themselves above the law.

Umberlee

Goddess of the seas

Overview

TitleGoddess of the seas
EpithetsThe Queen of the Depths, The Wavemother
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsTempest
SymbolA wave curling left and right
Home planeThe Abyss
Typical worshippersCoastal dwellers, sailors

Description

Umberlee is the goddess of the raging sea: shipwrecks, storms and sea monsters. People pray to her to spare a ship, and sailors throw her offerings before setting out. Her priests demand tribute in exchange for their protection, and her cult is powerful in the ports of the Sword Coast. She serves Talos.

Dogma

The sea is cruel and must be appeased. Pay tribute to Umberlee and never forget that the waters can swallow everything.

The faithful

Sailors pray to Umberlee before setting sail and throw coins, jewels or wine overboard to appease her wrath. Her true faithful behave like racketeers: they demand tribute from captains in exchange for their protection and threaten those who refuse to pay. They hold rites on beaches during storms and sometimes sacrifice sailors. They believe the sea is cruel and must be appeased. They hate Valkur and those who defy the sea without paying her homage.

Urdlen

God of greed and murder

Overview

TitleGod of greed and murder
EpithetsThe Crawler Below, The White Mole
PantheonGnomish pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsDeath, War
SymbolA clawed white mole emerging from the ground
Home planePandemonium
Typical worshippersEvil gnomes, murderers

Description

Urdlen is the gnome god of greed, murder and destruction. He is depicted as a giant blind mole. He is the enemy of the other gnome gods. His faithful are evil gnomes who commit murder and theft.

Dogma

Everything must be destroyed. Steal, kill and sow chaos.

The faithful

Urdlen's faithful are greedy and violent evil gnomes. They steal, kill and sow chaos in gnome communities. They often live hidden in tunnels. They believe everything must be destroyed. Their rites include sacrifices and acts of destruction.

Urogalan

God of earth and death

Overview

TitleGod of earth and death
EpithetsHe Who Must Be, The Lord in the Earth
PantheonHalfling pantheon
AlignmentLawful Neutral (LN)
Suggested domainsDeath, Knowledge
SymbolThe silhouette of a dog's head
Home planeThe Outlands
Typical worshippersHalflings, keepers of the dead

Description

Urogalan is the halfling god of earth and death. He protects the souls of the departed and watches over graves. His faithful organise funerals and comfort the families of the deceased.

Dogma

Death is a natural stage. Honour the dead, protect the graves and comfort the living.

The faithful

Urogalan's faithful are serious, calm and respectful of the dead. They organise funerals, protect graves and comfort families. They are often the only halflings who speak of death without fear. They believe death is a natural stage. Their rites are sober and take place underground.

Valkur

God of northern sailors

Overview

TitleGod of northern sailors
EpithetsThe Mighty, The Captain of the Waves
PantheonFaerûnian pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Good (CG)
Suggested domainsTempest, War
SymbolA cloud and three lightning bolts
Home planeYsgard
Typical worshippersSailors, captains, northern navigators

Description

Valkur is the god of sailors and ships, especially in the northern isles. He embodies courage in the face of the sea and camaraderie among crew members. Unlike Umberlee, whom he often confronts, he helps sailors rather than threatening them. Northerners worship him as a divine hero and recount his exploits in their songs.

Dogma

The sea is a challenge to be met. Face storms with courage, be loyal to your crew and protect ships against the dangers of the waves.

The faithful

Valkur's faithful are brave, loyal and cheerful sailors. They face storms bravely, protect their crew and refuse to abandon a companion who has fallen overboard. They sing sea shanties in his honour and celebrate every homecoming with rowdy feasts. They believe the sea is a challenge to be met rather than a threat to be appeased. They despise sailors who pay tribute to Umberlee, and oppose dishonourable pirates.

Vergadain

God of luck and wealth

Overview

TitleGod of luck and wealth
EpithetsThe Merchant King, The Laughing Dwarf
PantheonDwarven pantheon
AlignmentNeutral (N)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA gold coin stamped with a dwarf's face
Home planeThe Outlands
Typical worshippersDwarven merchants, traders, gamblers

Description

Vergadain is the dwarven god of trade, wealth and luck. Cunning and jovial, he loves a good deal and does not hesitate to dupe an overly naive customer. He is worshipped by dwarven merchants, who offer him a gold coin after every successful transaction. He represents commercial skill rather than Abbathor's pure greed.

Dogma

A good deal benefits whoever knows how to bargain. Be cunning, seize opportunities and share your luck with the clan.

The faithful

Vergadain's faithful are cunning, jovial and passionate about good deals. They trade skilfully, love haggling and do not hesitate to dupe a naive customer, which they see as a game rather than a crime. They offer their god a gold coin after every successful transaction and often carry a lucky coin. They believe luck and skill make wealth, and that a good merchant is useful to the whole clan. Their rites take place in markets and trading posts.

Vhaeraun

God of thieves

Overview

TitleGod of thieves
EpithetsThe Masked One, The Masked Lord
PantheonDrow pantheon
AlignmentChaotic Evil (CE)
Suggested domainsTrickery
SymbolA black mask with blue glass lenses over the eyes
Home planeThe Abyss
Typical worshippersDrow thieves, drow males, rebels

Description

Vhaeraun is the drow god of thieves, pride and rebellion against the matriarchy. A son of Lolth, he opposes her and preaches equality between drow men and women. He wants the drow to reclaim their place on the surface. His faithful are male thieves and rebels.

Dogma

The drow must free themselves from Lolth's tyranny. Steal, plot and give drow males back their place.

The faithful

Vhaeraun's faithful are rebel drow, often male, who reject Lolth's matriarchy. They steal, plot and seek to overthrow the priestesses. They often wear black masks and operate in secret, for they risk death if discovered. They believe drow males deserve equality and that the drow must reconquer the surface. Their rites are held in secret, at night, often on the surface.

Waukeen

Goddess of trade

Overview

TitleGoddess of trade

Description

Waukeen is the goddess of trade, wealth and exchange. She encourages the free movement of goods and ideas, and believes trade brings peoples together. She disappeared for a time during the Time of Troubles before returning. Her temples are often trading houses, and her priests serve as mediators and bankers.

Dogma

Trade enriches everyone. Encourage exchange, earn your fortune honestly and use your wealth to make your community prosper.

The faithful

Waukeen's faithful are shrewd, open-minded and pragmatic traders. They encourage trade, the free movement of goods and the prosperity of the community. They often serve as bankers, commercial arbiters or merchants, and their temples lend money to entrepreneurs. They believe trade enriches everyone and brings peoples together. They celebrate a successful deal with offerings of gold coins. They hate thieves, tyrants who impose excessive taxes and dishonest merchants.

Yondalla

Goddess of fertility and protection

TitleGoddess of fertility and protection
EpithetsThe Protector, The Provider

AlignmentLawful Good (LG)
Suggested domainsLife, Twilight
SymbolA cornucopia on a shield
Home planeBytopia (Green Fields)
Typical worshippersHalflings, families, protectors

Description

Yondalla is the mother and protector of the halflings. She is said to have created them and given them their legendary luck. She watches over halfling families, homes and communities. Her faithful are protectors and healers who watch over their people.

Dogma

Family and community are sacred. Protect your own, tend the land and share the abundance.

The faithful

Yondalla's faithful are protective, generous and attached to their community. They watch over families, tend the land and share the abundance with their neighbours. They believe family and community are sacred, and that no one should go hungry. Priests serve as advisers and mediators. Their rites take place at the hearth and during the great harvest festivals, with large shared meals.

Description

Yurtrus is the orc god of death and disease. He is silent and terrifying, and even the other orc gods fear him. His faithful are priests who keep silent and spread disease.

Dogma

Death awaits everyone. Fear it and serve it in silence.

The faithful

Yurtrus's faithful are silent and dreaded orc priests. They wear white gloves, never speak during their rites and tend to the dead. Even other orcs fear them. They believe death awaits everyone and that it must be served in silence.
